applies_to: Shinko WCL-13A two-loop controller with the C5 option; communication manual No.WCL1CE3.
summary: The WCL-13A is a two-channel PID temperature controller (one unit, two loops); CH1 also has a heat/cool OUT2. With the C5 option it speaks Shinko protocol, Modbus ASCII or Modbus RTU on RS485, and all items are signed 16-bit holding registers. The map covers both channels' SV, PID, alarm and output settings, shared timer and transmission settings, and each channel's PV, MV, SV, heater current and status words.

addressing.note: Registers are listed as hex data items (0001H) that go into the request unchanged. The manual's RTU example reads CH1 SV with data item 0001H, and its CRC (D5CAH) confirms 0001H is the wire address.

notes: CH2 items sit 50H above the matching CH1 items (SV 0001H vs 0051H); CH1-only OUT2 items have no CH2 twin. Read-only blocks start at 0080H (CH1) and 0090H (CH2); alarm 2-4 blocks at 00D0H (CH1) and 00E0H (CH2).
All data are 16-bit two's complement. Values with a decimal point are sent as whole numbers; apply each channel's decimal point place.
Input type codes differ between the multi-range and infrared thermocouple input versions, so value names are not listed.
PV may carry a difference or addition value when that block function is enabled in the console software.
Instrument number and speed can only be set on the keypad.

integration.summary: Select Modbus RTU with an 8-bit format on the keypad and set an instrument number. Poll 0080H-0083H for CH1 and 0090H-0093H for CH2 (PV, MV, SV, status); write SVs at 0001H and 0051H.
integration.enable: Requires the C5 option. Set Communication protocol to Modbus RTU and an 8-bit data bit/parity choice on the keypad, then the instrument number and speed.
quirks: Factory data format is 7 bits/Even; RTU needs an 8-bit choice.
SV temporary storage (002BH/007BH) is lost at power off; use SV (0001H/0051H) for permanent changes.
setup: Factory defaults: Shinko protocol, instrument 0, 9600 bps, 7 bits/Even, 1 stop bit.
gotchas: Non-volatile memory is rated about 1,000,000 writes; use the temporary SV for frequent setpoint changes.
